item.question_text: A team is deciding how far event-log keeping should reach across an AI system's life cycle. Which statement matches the Annex A control on recording event logs?

options.text: The organization determines the phases with event logging, expected at least while the system is in use.
The model supplier fixes the logging phases when handing over the technical documentation package.
Logging belongs with the verification and validation runs carried out in the period before release.
Logging is switched on once users have reported an incident during ordinary operation of the system.

item.explanation: A.6.2.8 places the decision with the organization and sets a floor: "The organization shall determine at which phases of the AI system life cycle, record keeping of event logs should be enabled, but at the minimum when the AI system is in use." The other options move the actor, the stage or the trigger.
item.key_support: The organization shall determine at which phases of the AI system life cycle, record keeping of event logs should be enabled, but at the minimum when the AI system is in use.

distractor_support.support: The organization shall determine at which phases of the AI system life cycle, record keeping of event logs should be enabled, but at the minimum when the AI system is in use.
distractor_support.why_wrong: The organization, not a supplier, determines the phases at which logging is enabled.

distractor_support.why_wrong: Confining logging to pre-release testing ignores the stated minimum of the in-use period.

distractor_support.why_wrong: Logging is tied to life-cycle phases decided in advance, not to an incident report.

item.question_text: A deployed classifier does not learn continuously, but its accuracy declines as the production data shifts, and the team prepares a retraining round. Which Annex A life-cycle control covers this activity?

options.text: Operation and monitoring, whose documented elements cover performance monitoring and updates
Verification and validation, whose documented measures come with criteria for their use
Deployment, whose documented plan confirms the applicable requirements before go-live
Technical documentation, whose content is matched to categories of interested parties

item.explanation: Detecting shifted performance in production and updating the system sits in the operation and monitoring stage. A.6.2.6 calls for documented elements for the ongoing running of the AI system, covering as a minimum the monitoring of the system and its performance, the fixing of faults, the issuing of updates and the provision of support. The other options name controls attached to earlier stages or to documentation provision.
item.key_support: At the minimum, this should include system and performance monitoring, repairs, updates and support.

distractor_support.support: and validation measures for the AI system and specify criteria for their use.
distractor_support.why_wrong: Verification and validation measures are set for testing the system, not for handling drift in live production data.

distractor_support.support: The organization shall document a deployment plan and ensure that appropriate requirements are met prior to deployment.
distractor_support.why_wrong: The deployment control addresses what happens ahead of go-live, not performance change during use.

distractor_support.support: documentation is needed for each relevant category of interested parties
distractor_support.why_wrong: This control concerns determining and supplying technical documentation, not monitoring or retraining.

item.question_text: A system already in production is to receive a substantial functional upgrade. Which statement reflects the Annex A control on AI system requirements and specification?

options.text: Requirements are specified and documented for the upgrade, just as for a newly built system.
Requirements documents are prepared for new builds; upgrades are handled under the deployment plan.
Requirements are captured inside the design and development documentation rather than separately.
Requirements for the upgrade are conveyed through the technical documentation given to users.

item.explanation: A.6.2.2 extends the requirements control beyond first builds: it reaches both brand-new systems and significant upgrades to systems already in place. The distractors displace that work onto deployment planning, design documentation or user-facing technical documentation.
item.key_support: for new AI systems or material enhancements to existing systems.

distractor_support.support: for new AI systems or material enhancements to existing systems.
distractor_support.why_wrong: Material enhancements are explicitly inside the scope of the requirements control, not covered by deployment planning alone.

distractor_support.support: The organization shall document the AI system design and and development development based on organizational objectives, docu- mented requirements and specification criteria.
distractor_support.why_wrong: Design and development documentation is built on documented requirements, so it presupposes rather than replaces them.

distractor_support.support: documentation is needed for each relevant category of interested parties
distractor_support.why_wrong: Technical documentation is provided to interested parties and is not the vehicle for specifying requirements.

item.question_text: A validated model is about to be released into a cloud environment. Which item does Annex A place at the deployment stage?

options.text: A documented deployment plan, with the applicable requirements satisfied beforehand
A documented record of design choices resting on the specification criteria
A documented decision on which life-cycle phases keep records of events
A documented set of objectives steering responsible development of the system

item.explanation: Clause A.6.2.5 places two things at this stage: a written plan for the deployment, and confirmation that the relevant requirements have been satisfied before the system goes live. The other options belong to design documentation (A.6.2.3), event-log phases (A.6.2.8) and development objectives (A.6.1.2).
item.key_support: The organization shall document a deployment plan and ensure that appropriate requirements are met prior to deployment.

distractor_support.support: The organization shall document the AI system design and and development development based on organizational objectives, docu- mented requirements and specification criteria.

distractor_support.support: The organization shall determine at which phases of the AI system life cycle, record keeping of event logs should be enabled, but at the minimum when the AI system is in use.
distractor_support.why_wrong: The logging-phase decision is a separate control and is not what the deployment control calls for.

distractor_support.support: Objectives for responsible develop- The organization shall identify and document objectives ment of AI system to guide the responsible development AI systems, and take those objectives into account and integrate measures to achieve them in the development life cycle.
distractor_support.why_wrong: Responsible development objectives are set for the development life cycle, not as the deployment-stage item.

item.question_text: An auditor asks why AIMS obligations are spread across stages instead of concentrating at release. Which description best captures the stated aim of the AI system life cycle control set?

options.text: Setting the criteria and requirements that apply at each separate stage
Gathering evidence from earlier work into a single release decision
Tracking where data came from across the data and system life cycles
Documenting objectives and processes for responsible design and development

item.explanation: The objective stated at B.6.2.1 for this control set is to establish, stage by stage, what the criteria and requirements are across the AI system life cycle, which is why obligations attach at every stage rather than only at release. The other options restate the aim of data provenance, restate the aim of the responsible development guidance, or collapse the life cycle into a single release gate.
item.key_support: To define the criteria and requirements for each stage of the AI system life cycle.

distractor_support.support: To define the criteria and requirements for each stage of the AI system life cycle.
distractor_support.why_wrong: The stated aim is stage-by-stage criteria, not evidence funnelled into one release decision.

distractor_support.support: Data provenance The organization shall define and document a process for recording the provenance of data used in its AI systems over the life cycles of the data and the AI system.
distractor_support.why_wrong: This is the aim of the data provenance control, not of the life cycle control set.

distractor_support.support: To ensure that the organization identifies and documents objectives and implements processes for the responsible design and development of AI systems.
distractor_support.why_wrong: This is the objective of the management guidance for development, a different control set.
